content.thinking:
Checking the search index table name, webhook scheduler timing, toIssue mapper, ActionResult type, and whether getDb uses SQLite.

Also checking whether incrementUsage throws when no usage row exists. Reviewing the scheduler for webhook delivery timing. Looking at session repository token lookup. Noting that resolving the actor on every action triggers a side effect: memberRepo.touchLastSeen updates last_seen_at.

Confirmed createIssueAction is the only entry point for issue creation. Client-side Zod validation runs before submission, and the server re-parses with the same schema. Several fields in the schema use .default().

The form omits parentId and estimate, so those fields remain at schema defaults unless defaultValues override them. Title must be 3 to 200 characters. Description is capped at 20000 characters or null. Status defaults to backlog. Priority defaults to none. AssigneeId and dueAt are nullable. LabelIds are limited to 20 ULIDs.

The form derives orgId, projectId, and status from org settings via defaultStatusFor. Because defaultValues are spread with the last argument winning, the organization's defaultIssueStatus overrides the schema's backlog default. The input object includes hidden orgId and projectId fields. During actor resolution, requireActorFor receives only an orgId string with no orgSlug, so it calls getSessionPrincipal and throws UnauthorizedError if null or NoMembershipError if activeOrgId is missing.

Membership is verified against the organization slug from the payload, not the activeOrgId. The activeOrgId is only checked for null. The actor's orgId comes from the organization looked up by the payload orgId.

The active-org check is not a strict equality match. A signed-in member of organization B can create an issue in organization A if they have an active membership there, provided their session carries a non-null activeOrgId.

The action's can() guard verifies actor.orgId matches the issue's orgId. The service also reasserts org scope. touchLastSeen writes occur before the issue write during actor resolution.

Also checking the activity table name and how the webhook job is registered in the scheduler.

UnauthorizedError maps to internal_error via toAppError. Zod errors produce a validation_failed ActionResult, and stamp() overwrites submittedAt when converting to an action result.

AlreadyArchivedError is thrown by assertNotArchived when the project is archived and maps to conflict. NotFoundError for missing projects or organizations becomes internal_error with a message like "Project {id} was not found". PlanLimitError preserves its message as internal_error. PermissionDeniedError maps to forbidden. Generic errors from wouldExceedLimit map to internal_error.

The client receives mapped error messages through ErrorMessage. On failure it calls setError(result.error). On success it resets the form to defaultValues. The scheduler runs webhook delivery as an async follow-up job. Usage rollup is a later correction. Synchronous consequences are handled by event subscribers.

The search reindex job does not run on issue creation. The inline listener handles indexing immediately.

The notification service ignores issue.created events. Assignees are stored but not notified at creation time.

Labels are inserted into the issue_labels junction table only when labelIds is non-empty.

Checking the `toIssue` mapping for `archivedAt`. The insert operation does not explicitly set this nullable column.

Confirmed `getDb` uses synchronous better-sqlite3. The action ordering is correct: issue creation requires member, then summary needs org:read for viewers, then listIssues needs issue:read. Archived issues count toward the action's quota ceiling because the limit check queries with `includeArchived: true`.

The service-level quota check only counts live issues, so it can allow creation when archived issues have already filled the action limit. Both gates run in sequence on the form path. Enterprise plans set issuesPerProject to Infinity, so both checks pass.

Free, starter, and growth plans cap issues at 100, 1000, and 10000 respectively. The page-level gate hides the form when the limit is reached, but the Server Action re-checks it on submission. The client path runs Zod validation in IssueForm, then submits to createIssueAction.

The Server Action uses `withAction` from `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`. Handlers run via `Promise.allSettled`, so a subscriber failure does not roll back the issue insert. The insert commits before subscribers execute, and any subscriber error is swallowed by the emit layer. The action still returns the created issue.

A signed-in member submitting the new-issue form ends in `createIssueAction`. The browser validates first, the action resolves an `Actor` and re-checks permission and quota, `createIssue` writes the row, and `issue.created` then updates the audit log, the search index, the usage counter, and the webhook queue.

## Browser

The page at `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/new/page.tsx` renders `IssueForm` (`src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx`) with `onSubmit={createIssueAction}`. The form is a client component. `useForm` uses `zodResolver(createIssueSchema)` from `src/schemas/issue.ts`, so the same schema the server will parse also blocks the submit in the browser.

`createIssueSchema` requires a ULID `orgId` and `projectId`, a title of 3–200 characters, an optional description up to 20,000 characters, a status (`issueStatusSchema`, default `"backlog"`), a priority (default `"none"`), a nullable `assigneeId`, a nullable `parentId`, a nullable integer `estimate` from 0 to 100, a nullable ISO `dueAt`, and at most 20 `labelIds`. The page seeds `status` from `org.settings.defaultIssueStatus` through `defaultStatusFor`, which re-parses that string with `issueStatusSchema` and falls back to `"backlog"`. The form does not render parent or estimate, so those stay `null`. The author is not a form field.

On submit, `form.handleSubmit` calls `submit` from `useFormAction` (`src/hooks/use-form-action.ts`). That sets `pending`, awaits the Server Action, and expects an `ActionResult<Issue>` (`src/types/api.ts`). A thrown error is normalized with `toAppError`.

The POST still passes `proxy` in `src/proxy.ts`. For a non-public path it only checks that the `taskflow_session` cookie exists. If it does, the request continues with the `x-taskflow-authenticated` header. Role and membership are not decided there.

## Server Action wrapper

`createIssueAction` in `src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts` is the `"use server"` entry. It delegates to `run`, built by `withAction` in `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`.

1. `createIssueSchema.safeParse(raw)` runs again. Failure returns `toActionResult` (`src/lib/errors.ts`): `code: "validation_failed"`, message `"Please correct the highlighted fields."`, and `fieldErrors`. `stamp` adds `submittedAt`. The handler never runs.
2. `resolveActorFor` sees `orgId` on the parsed `CreateIssueInput` and calls `requireActorFor` (`src/lib/actor.ts`). There is no `orgSlug` on this payload.

`requireActorFor` builds the `Actor` (`src/types/member.ts`: `userId`, `orgId`, `role`, optional `isPlatformStaff`):

- `getSessionPrincipal` (`src/lib/session.ts`) reads the cookie and calls `resolveSession` (`src/server/services/session-service.ts`), which hashes the token with `hashToken` and loads `sessionRepo.findSessionByTokenHash`. That joins `sessions` to `users` and returns a `SessionPrincipal` only while `expiresAt` is still in the future. `getSessionPrincipal` checks the expiry a second time. No principal throws `UnauthorizedError`.
- `activeOrgId === null` throws `NoMembershipError`. The check is only that some active org is set. It does not require that id to equal the payload org.
- `findOrgById` loads the organization named by the payload. A missing org throws `NoMembershipError`.
- `resolveActorForOrg(principal, org.slug)` loads the org by slug, then `memberRepo.findMember`. The membership must exist and have `status === "active"`. The resulting `Actor` is `{ userId, orgId: org.id, role: member.role }` with no `isPlatformStaff`. `assertOrgScope` (`src/lib/tenant.ts`) then requires `actor.orgId === org.id`, and `memberRepo.touchLastSeen` writes `members.last_seen_at`.
- `requireActorFor` calls `assertOrgScope` once more against the payload `orgId`.

Anything thrown here is caught by `withAction` and returned through `toActionResult`. `UnauthorizedError`, `NoMembershipError`, `ForbiddenActionError`, `PlanLimitError`, and `NotFoundError` are not special cases in `toAppError`, so they come back as `internal_error` with the error’s message. `PermissionDeniedError` maps to `forbidden`, `AlreadyArchivedError` to `conflict`, `TenantScopeError` to `tenant_scope_violation`.

## Gates inside the action

The handler in `create-issue.ts` then runs three checks of its own.

**Permission.** `can(actor, "issue:create", issueResource)` (`src/lib/permissions.ts`) is called with a synthetic issue resource: `kind: "issue"`, the payload org and project, an empty `issueId`, `authorId: actor.userId`, and the chosen `assigneeId`. `explain` decides in order: `actor.orgId` must equal `resource.orgId` (`denied_cross_tenant` otherwise); `isPlatformStaff` would allow it, but this actor does not have that flag; `ROLE_MATRIX["issue:create"]` is `"member"`, so `ROLE_RANK` must be at least `member` (2). Owner and admin pass. Viewer fails with `denied_by_role`. `issue:create` is not in `OWNERSHIP_ESCALATIONS`. Failure throws `ForbiddenActionError`.

**Plan quota.** `assertProjectHasRoom` calls `getOrganizationSummary` (`src/server/services/organization-service.ts`), which again runs `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan(actor, "org:read", …)` (`org:read` is allowed for `viewer` and above), then loads the organization, `usageRepo.getUsage`, the active member count, and the project count. `getPlanLimits(summary.organization.plan)` (`src/config/plan-limits.ts`) supplies `issuesPerProject`: 100 on free, 1,000 on starter, 10,000 on growth, and `Infinity` on enterprise. `listIssues` (`issue-service.ts`) runs `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource)` and then `issueRepo.listIssues` with `includeArchived: true` and `limit: 1`. The limit only shortens the page; `existing.total` is the full count, archived rows included. If `existing.total >= limits.issuesPerProject`, it throws `PlanLimitError("issuesPerProject", limit, total)`.

**Write.** `createIssue(actor, input)` is next.

## Service gates, then the row

`createIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` applies four more gates before it allocates a number:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)`.
2. `projectRepo.findProjectById(input.orgId, input.projectId)` (`src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts`) filters on `org_id` and `id`. `requireFound` (`src/server/services/_support.ts`) throws `NotFoundError` when the project is missing. `assertNotArchived` (`src/lib/soft-delete.ts`) throws `AlreadyArchivedError` when `archivedAt` is set.
3. `assertCan(actor, "issue:create", projectResource(project))`. This is the same `issue:create` / `member` rule, this time against a `kind: "project"` resource carrying `visibility` and `leadId`. `explain` does not consult visibility. A denial throws `PermissionDeniedError`.
4. `orgRepo.findOrgById` must find the organization. `issueRepo.countIssues` counts only live rows (`livePredicate` / `archived_at IS NULL`, because the default `ArchiveScope` omits archived issues). `wouldExceedLimit(org.plan, "issuesPerProject", used)` is `used + 1 > limit`. A breach throws a plain `Error` naming the plan and the project key.

No gate checks that the assignee is a member, that `parentId` exists, or that each label belongs to the org.

`issueRepo.nextIssueNumber` takes `max(number)` over every issue in the project, archived included, and adds 1. `insertIssue` (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`) writes one row through `getDb()` (`src/server/db/client.ts`, better-sqlite3, WAL, foreign keys on). The `issues` table is defined in `src/server/db/schema/issues.ts`. The inserted `IssueRow` / `NewIssueRow` is:

- `id`: a ULID from `newId()` (`src/lib/id.ts`)
- `org_id`, `project_id`, `number`
- `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority` from the input
- `author_id`: `actor.userId`
- `assignee_id`, `parent_id`, `estimate`, `due_at` from the input
- `started_at` and `completed_at`: `null`, even when the status is `in_progress`, `done`, or `canceled` (those stamps are maintained only by `setIssueStatus`)
- `created_at` and `updated_at`: one shared ISO timestamp
- `archived_at`: left null

The unique index `issues_project_number_idx` is on `(project_id, number)`. If `labelIds` is non-empty, a second statement inserts into `issue_labels` (`org_id`, `issue_id`, `label_id`), unique on `(issue_id, label_id)`. The schema declares no foreign keys on those columns, so the two statements are not wrapped in a transaction. `toIssue` (`src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts`) returns the `Issue` domain object with `labelIds` attached.

## What `issue.created` causes

`createIssue` then `await emit("issue.created", …)` (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`). The payload is an `EventEnvelope` (`orgId`, `actorId`, `occurredAt`) plus `issueId`, `projectId`, `title`, `assigneeId`, and `priority` (`src/types/event.ts`). `actorEnvelope` fills the envelope from the actor. Subscribers were attached once per process by `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, called from `register()` in `src/instrumentation.ts`. `emit` runs every handler with `Promise.allSettled`. A handler that throws is reported to the error sinks and does not fail the action or undo the insert.

Four listeners handle this event:

- `registerActivityListeners` (`src/server/services/activity-service.ts`) calls `record`, which `activityRepo.insertActivity` appends to `activity_events`: action `"issue.created"`, subject kind `"issue"`, the issue and project ids, summary `Created issue "<title>"`, and metadata `{ priority }`.
- `registerSearchListeners` (`src/server/services/search-service.ts`) re-reads the issue with `findIssueById` and `indexIssue` upserts `search_index` (`src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`) for subject kind `"issue"`, content `title + "\n" + description`, and the project id.
- `registerUsageListeners` (`src/server/services/usage-service.ts`) calls `usageRepo.incrementUsage(orgId, { issuesUsed: 1 })`, which adds one to `organization_usage.issues_used` and refreshes `measured_at`. This path does not call `recomputeUsage`, so it does not emit `billing.limit_exceeded`.
- `registerWebhookListeners` (`src/server/services/webhook-service.ts`) calls `enqueueForOrg`. For each enabled row in `webhook_endpoints` whose `event_types` JSON includes `"issue.created"`, `webhookRepo.enqueueDelivery` inserts a `webhook_deliveries` row with status `"pending"`.

`registerFanOut` in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` subscribes to `issue.assigned`, `issue.overdue`, `comment.created`, and `member.joined`. The create path emits only `issue.created`, so an assignee stored on the new row gets no notification row and no email.

Later, the scheduler started from `instrumentation.ts` (`src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`) enqueues `webhook-delivery` about once a minute. `runWebhookDeliveryJob` claims pending deliveries, refuses orgs whose plan does not include webhooks, and records a delivery by computing `signPayload` (HMAC-SHA256 of the body). The usage rollup later recounts `issuesUsed` from the source tables. The daily search-reindex job is separate from this inline index write.

## Response and the form

Back in the action, `revalidateTagged` (`src/lib/cache.ts`) invalidates `org:<orgId>`, `project:<projectId>`, and `issue:<issueId>` under the `"minutes"` cache profile. `withAction` then invalidates the static tag `"issues"` under the same profile, and `stamp` returns `{ ok: true, data: issue, submittedAt }`.

`useFormAction` clears the error and runs `form.reset()`, which restores the page’s default values. The member stays on the new-issue page. A failure result is shown by `ErrorMessage` from `error.message`.
